session_notes:
Two qubits (qA1, qA2), ten runs: one vs_power map in the morning (#17, 05:52), eight 1-D sweeps in the evening (#53-#60, 21:43-21:51), one more vs_power map at the very end (#61, 21:57). The session ENDS ON A WRONG ANSWER for both qubits, and the mechanism is not one of the usual suspects.

WHAT #17 ACTUALLY SHOWED (it is the good run of the session). 100 MHz span, 0.25 MHz step, powers -55..-20 dBm. Reading the map as a physicist: for both qubits the line is at the resolution floor (about two pixels wide) and its position is STATIONARY over the lower two thirds of the swept powers, then it broadens monotonically (roughly 0.5 -> 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 MHz across the power axis) and starts to AC-Stark shift near the top (qA2 drifts up, qA1 drifts down - the two qubits shift in OPPOSITE directions, which is itself useful: a shift both share is an artifact, not physics). Sub-pixel centroids of the low-power block give qA2 = 5.71519 GHz and qA1 = 5.07513 GHz, matching the node's own numbers to within a few kHz. So #17's frequencies are trustworthy despite its power_warning="sweep_too_hot" and despite relative_freq being exactly 0.0 for both targets - both flags fired, and the MAP refutes both.

THE FLAGS, ONE BY ONE. success=True on every target of every run in this session and means nothing, as the corpus statistic says. power_warning="sweep_too_hot" on #17 is true by the node's own criterion (the line never faded at the bottom of the sweep) but harmless here, because the diagnostic that matters - is the track flat and is the width at the frequency-step floor - passes. relative_freq exactly 0.0 on #17 is the centre-returned SIGNATURE without the centre-returned failure: the map has an unmistakable feature sitting on the centre, i.e. the benign "the qubit has not moved" case the caution covers. fringe_detected=True on both vs_power runs is a FALSE positive in both: #17's fringe marker sits at the noisiest, lowest-power end where peak height is scatter-dominated, and #61's sits on the detection knee - neither figure shows the smooth height oscillation with power that real pi/2pi/3pi fringing produces.

THE QUBIT MOVED DURING THE DAY (qA2 only). Between #17 and #53 the chip went through flux-distortion and ramsey-vs-flux work (#34-#51) and a resonator-vs-flux run (#52). qA2's line is genuinely at 5.71519 GHz in the morning and genuinely at ~5.71545 GHz in the evening - independent Lorentzian fits of the evening raw traces find the peak there, and the morning value lay well inside every evening span, so it was not missed. qA1 did not move (5.07513 -> 5.07512). The end-of-session answer therefore has to come from the evening data for qA2.

WHY #61 IS WRONG, AND IT IS NOT THE TWO-PHOTON LINE. #61 swept 500 MHz at a 1.5 MHz STEP - roughly twice the low-power linewidth measured in #17. Re-binning #17's own fine cube onto a 1.5 MHz grid retains only 32-63% of the true peak height at the bottom of the power axis but 83-91% at the top, because a coarse grid steps over a narrow line and cannot step over a broad one. That power-dependent dilution MANUFACTURES AN ONSET: #61's fringe/height diagnostic is flat at the noise floor up to about -48 dBm and only then rises, so the node cleared its sweep_too_hot warning (power_warning is empty on #61, the only run in the session where it is) and concluded it had bracketed the onset. It then chose a drive 12 dB (qA2) and 19 dB (qA1) hotter than #17 had chosen, read the centre off a 3.7 / 4.4 MHz-wide line (intrinsic 1.8 / 2.3 MHz, i.e. fwhm/intrinsic about 2.0 - at the corpus p90) sampled on 1.5 MHz pixels, and returned relative_freq = +500000.0 Hz EXACTLY for both qubits. Exactly the same round number on two different qubits is the tell: a real AC-Stark shift at that power would be up for qA2 and DOWN for qA1, which is what #17's map says. Both values were written to state (confirmed in #61's and #62's quam_state) and both are about +0.5 MHz too high. The saturation drive also ended the session at 64% and 90% of full scale.

CONTRIBUTORY: the operator's own ramp. The 1-D node ran with target_peak_width = 3 MHz, so each accepted run raised the saturation amplitude toward a deliberately broadened line: the applied drive walks -55 dBm (#53) -> -52 (#55, #57) -> -49 (#58) -> -43 (#59) -> -35 (#60), and #17's broadening curve predicts every one of those measured linewidths (0.5, 0.8, 0.8, 1.0-1.2, 2.2-2.7 MHz). #61 then started from that hot state. The broadening was chosen on purpose for robustness; it is the wrong regime for reading a frequency.

THE TWO-PHOTON TRAP WAS ARMED BUT NEVER SPRUNG. #61's 500 MHz span is the only sweep in the session wide enough to contain the 0->2 line, and it is there for both qubits, half the run's own reported anharmonicity below the fundamental (measured ratio 0.496 and 0.497). It grows faster with power than the fundamental exactly as the family says - its height relative to the fundamental goes from about 0.02 in the middle third of the power axis to 0.08 (qA2) and 0.18 (qA1) in the hottest third. No fit in this session landed on it: the 1-D spans (17 to 50 MHz half-width) do not even reach it. For qA1 the node fitted it correctly and returned an anharmonicity within 0.07% of the stored value, which is the one genuinely useful product of #61.

WHAT A CAREFUL OPERATOR NEEDED: #17 for the map, the power decision and the anharmonicity context, then one well-resolved 1-D at that power after the day's flux work - #58 (35 MHz span, 0.1 MHz step, drive about -49 dBm, the narrowest lines and the best fits of the eight). #53-#57 were span/step/amplitude hunting, #59-#60 were over-driven, and #61 was worse than useless: it overwrote two good frequencies with two bad ones.
adversarial_audit:
## Verdict

**The key's answers are right; a large part of its reasoning is not.** Both `final_frequency_hz` values are well supported, both tolerances accept every properly-powered run and reject the session's actual wrong answer, and `ideal_runs = [17, 58]` is chronologically legal. But the central explanation of *why* #61 is wrong is misdiagnosed, one stated mechanism is contradicted by the node parameters, one piece of cited evidence is false, one `traps_present` entry contradicts the key's own text, and several arithmetic and corpus-statistic claims do not survive recomputation. I would keep the numbers and rewrite the narrative.

---

## Defects

**1. The reason #61 returns +500000.0 Hz is not the one given — and it is decisive.** #61's detuning axis is `arange(-250 MHz, +250 MHz, 1.5 MHz)`; **zero detuning is not a grid point.** From `ds_fit.h5`: `detuning` contains no 0, and the two samples nearest zero are `-1000000` and `+500000`. `+500000.0` is simply the nearest available sample to "no change", for both qubits, necessarily. The key instead builds its case on "exactly the same round number on two different qubits is the tell ... no shared physical shift can produce it", which is true but is answering a question the grid already closed. For contrast, #17's grid (0.25 MHz step) *does* contain 0, which is why its `freq_shift = 0.0` means something different — the key gets that half right without noticing it is the same fact.

**2. The power-broadening half of the #61 diagnosis is refuted by #61's own fit file.** The key says #61 "read the centre off a 3.66 MHz-wide line ... in a power-broadened regime" and that the hot drive is what produced the error. `ds_fit.h5:peak_position` for #61 is `+0.5 MHz` at essentially every power row from the first one where a peak was detected (index 23, −46.9 dBm) to the top. Block means: qA2 mid-third `+0.182 MHz`, hot-third `+0.015 MHz`; qA1 `+0.227` and `−0.206`. The reported centre is the same cold as hot. Had the node chosen −47 dBm it would have written the identical +500 kHz. The hot power is a real defect of #61, but it is not what makes the frequency wrong.

**3. "The two qubits shift in OPPOSITE directions" is not in the data.** From #17's `peak_position` track (250 kHz grid, 100 rows): qA2 top-third mean **−59 kHz**, top-10 mean **−100 kHz**; qA1 top-third mean **−132 kHz**, top-10 mean **+150 kHz**. Both tracks are ±250 kHz to ±1.5 MHz scatter with no monotone drift either way. At the exact powers #61 chose (row 57 for qA2, row 71 for qA1) the local means are +36 kHz and −36 kHz — noise. The qA1 text ("moves DOWN by roughly a quarter of a MHz in the hottest blocks and by nearly a MHz at the very top, qA2's moves up") reads a single last row (`pp[qA1,99] = −1.0 MHz`) out of a tail that also contains +2.0, −2.5, +2.0; qA2's last row is **−0.5 MHz**, i.e. down, not up. This is the key's headline argument and it is cherry-picked.

**4. `traps_present` includes `stark_shifted`, which the key's own reasoning denies.** The qA2 section states "no monotone power trend, so scatter and not Stark shift dominates", and the whole #61 argument is that the offset is an artifact. Nothing in the session demonstrates a sprung Stark-shift trap. Ironically, the one power-monotone trend that *does* exist is one the key explicitly denies: qA2's three fine-step runs at −48.9 / −43.0 / −35.0 dBm give 5,715,387,780 → 5,715,446,272 → 5,715,483,411, a clean +58 kHz then +37 kHz with power, in the only three evening runs with r-squared above 0.92.

**5. "each accepted run raised the saturation amplitude" is false — the node never wrote an amplitude.** Every 1-D run in the session carries `update_pulses_amplitude: False`, and every figure prints `sat amp = … (not applied)`. The state's saturation amplitude is pinned at 0.0025449 (qA2) / 0.0023127 (qA1) from #21 all the way through #58. The ramp is entirely manual: `operation_amplitude_factor` 1.0 → 1.25 → 1.5 → 1.5 → 1.5 → 2.0 across #53–#58, then the operator hand-typed the state amplitude to **0.0100 (#59) and 0.0250 (#60) — the same value for both qubits**, which no per-qubit fit would produce, and neither matching the node's own recommendation (#58 recommended 0.009429 / 0.013183; #59 recommended 0.029661 / 0.024586). The key's conclusion ("the operator's own ramp") is right; its stated mechanism is not. Relatedly, only **#56, #58, #60 and #61** ever reached the state — chaining each run's `relative_freq` back to its pre-run centre shows #60's centre is #58's output (5,715,387,780), not #59's (5,715,446,272), so #59, which the key counts in the ramp, contributed nothing. #53/#54/#55/#57/#59 were never applied.

**6. "the evening raw data has no peak at the morning frequency" is false.** In #58's raw trace the rotated-I excursion **at** the morning frequency 5,715,188,534 is **94% of the peak value and 36 sigma above baseline noise**; the separation from #58's fitted centre is 199 kHz = **0.25 FWHM**. The two frequencies are not separable in that data. The qA2 move is real, but the evidence for it is the ramsey-vs-flux chain (see next), not the evening spectroscopy.

**7. The flux bias changed and the key never says so.** `qubits/*/z/joint_offset` goes 0.0019567 → 0.0109087 (qA2) and 0.0041749 → 0.0103107 (qA1) between #17 and #53 — moved by #39–#51 and then bumped a further +0.002 V by hand before #53. That is why qA2 moved, and the ramsey chain independently walked qA2's estimate 5,715,188,534 → 5,715,463,634 (+275 kHz) across #42–#51 with no spectroscopy involved. This is much stronger evidence than what the key cites. It also means "#17's broadening curve correctly predicts the measured linewidth of every later 1-D run" is a cross-bias-point comparison the key does not flag.

**8. "ratio 2.0 — at the corpus p90" is wrong.** The family text itself gives median 1.39 / p90 2.50. Recomputing over the whole index (242 vs_power targets in `sessions.json`) gives median 1.568, p90 2.583, max 5.198; #61's 1.994 and 1.951 sit at the **74th and 73rd percentiles**. Above median, nowhere near p90. The mis-citation makes #61 look more anomalous than it is.

**9. qA1: "The whole body of evidence sits inside a +/-40 kHz band around 5.075125 GHz" is arithmetically false.** The key's own nine cited values run from 5,075,053,254 (07-26 #240) to 5,075,138,008 (07-24) — **−71.7 kHz to +13.0 kHz, an 85 kHz spread**, with two values outside ±40 kHz.

**10. qA2: the evening statistics do not reproduce, and the adopted centre is not the stated mean.** The six free fits quoted (5.715421, .481, .551, .532, .446, .483) have **mean 5.7154857 and sample std 49 kHz**, not "mean 5.71547 ... scatter about 60-85 kHz". Having stated 5.71547, the key then adopts **5.71542** as "the centre of that body of evidence" — 50 kHz lower, unexplained. The direction matters: the lower centre is what buys the margin by which #61 is rejected. Separately, the key declares "anything in 5.71539–5.71548 GHz is equally right" while its own designated best measurement, #58, sits at 5,715,387,780 — 2.2 kHz *below* that window.

**11. Node values and the auditor's re-fits are mixed without labelling.** "#53 5.715421, #54 5.715481" are re-fits; the archive reports **5.715339** and **5.715589** (82 and 108 kHz away). My own independent Lorentzians give 5.715434 and 5.715507, so the key's re-fits are defensible — but nothing tells the reader these are not archive numbers. The same mixing infects the linewidth ramp "(0.5, 0.8, 0.8, 1.0-1.2, 2.2-2.7 MHz)": **#53's node-reported FWHM is 1.225 MHz for both qubits and #56's is 1.960 MHz — larger than #58's 0.810 MHz at 6 dB more power.** Read from node outputs the monotone-broadening story is simply broken; it only holds on re-fits. "#17's broadening curve predicts every one of those measured linewidths" never says which "measured" it means.

**12. "#58 ... FWHM 0.79 MHz" (qA2) is wrong.** `data.json` and the run's own figure both say **0.810 MHz** (809,662 Hz). The derived tolerance (400 kHz, half of 0.810) survives; the quoted number does not. The qA1 figures (0.526 MHz, snr 25, r-squared 0.946) are exact.

**13. "ended the session at 64% and 90% of full scale" is the wrong base.** The end-of-session amplitudes are 0.0642060 and 0.0901676, i.e. **6.4% and 9.0% of full scale** in QUAM's convention; 64% / 90% is the fraction of the node's `max_amp = 0.1` cap. The key also omits that #61 lowered `full_scale_power_dbm` from −3 to **−11 (qA2) / −9 (qA1)** in the same write, which is what actually sets the absolute −34.85 / −29.90 dBm.

**14. qA1's 07-24 corroboration is not independent.** #117 and #118 both return `relative_freq = 0.0` and the *identical* frequency 5,075,138,007.6 — neither moved the prior. They corroborate the state estimate, not a measurement. That is exactly the centre-returned signature the key applies so carefully to #17 and #55–#57, applied nowhere here. (#116's qA1 fit returned NaN outright; also unmentioned.)

**15. Smaller overstatements.** (a) "#61's [fringe marker] sits on the detection knee" — true for qA1 (−46.9 dBm, exactly the knee), wrong for qA2 (−40.9 dBm, ~6 dB above the knee on a local notch). (b) "the low-power end of the map went flat at the noise floor" — the line is still there; block-averaging #61's lower third gives a 0.00097 excursion against 0.00005 noise. What actually failed is the node's per-row fit, which returns NaN `peak_position` below row 23 (qA2) / 19 (qA1). (c) "broadens monotonically (roughly 0.5 -> 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 MHz)" — #17's `peak_width` medians by third are 0.49 / 1.57 / 2.99 (qA2) and 0.54 / 1.70 / 3.70 (qA1), with track maxima of 5.5 and 6.9 MHz; the top is overstated ~2x and the track is not monotone row-to-row (qA2: 3.04 MHz at row 65, 1.29 at row 66). (d) "1.5 MHz step is about twice the low-power linewidth measured in #17" — for qA2 #17 measured 0.460 MHz, so 3.3x. (e) sub-pixel centroids quoted as 5.715183–5.715192 (9 kHz) and 5.075128–5.075144 (16 kHz); reproducing with both centroids and Lorentzian fits over several low-power blocks I get 5.715174–5.715218 and 5.075085–5.075166 — right region, spread 3-5x wider than claimed. (f) "#58 ... the narrowest lines and the best fits of the eight" — true for qA1 on every metric; for qA2 #57's FWHM is 16 Hz narrower and #58's r-squared and snr are beaten by #59 and #60. #58 is still the correct pick, just not by those criteria. (g) "power_warning is empty on #61, the only run in the session where it is" — the 1-D runs have no such field at all, so this is 1-of-2 vs_power runs.

**16. `ideal_runs` does not produce `final_frequency_hz` for qA2.** #17 reports 5,715,188,534 and #58 reports 5,715,387,780; the answer is 5,715,420,000, obtained by averaging in #53–#57, #59 and #60 — runs the key itself dismisses as "span/step/amplitude hunting" and "over-driven". An operator running exactly [17, 58] lands at 5,715,388, which is 32 kHz from the stated answer and comfortably inside tolerance, so this is not a scoring failure — but the ideal path and the answer are derived from different evidence sets.

**17. Tolerance caveats.** Both tolerances behave as claimed, with two qualifications. qA2's ±400 kHz also **accepts #17's morning value** (231 kHz off), so the target cannot test its own central claim that the qubit moved — and given defect 6 (the move is a quarter linewidth), that may be the honest outcome, but it deserves stating rather than being left as an aside. Second, "rejects #61's answer by a clear margin (563 kHz off)" and "rejects #61 by 510 kHz" quote the offset from centre, not the margin beyond tolerance, which is **163 kHz (qA2)** and **250 kHz (qA1)**. For qA2 that is 0.2 of the very linewidth the tolerance was built from, and it is sensitive to the unexplained 50 kHz centre shift in defect 10.

---

## What held up under re-derivation

I want to be clear about how much of this key is correct, because most of it is.

Run inventory, timestamps, and the #34–#51 / #52 characterisation are all right. #17's parameters (100 MHz span, 0.25 MHz step, −55…−20 dBm, 100 points) and #61's (500 MHz, 1.5 MHz, same power axis) are exact. #17's line really is at the resolution floor (lower-third median width 0.49 / 0.54 MHz, about two pixels) and really is stationary over the lower two thirds (track mean −11 kHz for both qubits). `sweep_too_hot` on #17 is correct by the node's criterion — the fringe figure shows the peak height already saturated at −55 dBm and never falling — and the map really does refute the centre-returned worry, since #17's grid does contain 0 and an unmistakable narrow feature sits on it. `fringe_detected` on both vs_power runs is a false positive; neither height-vs-power curve oscillates.

The re-binning mechanism is real and I reproduced it: averaging #17's own cube down to a 1.5 MHz grid gives peak-height retention of **0.28–0.73 (mean 0.43)** at the bottom of the power axis versus **0.68–0.93 (mean 0.79)** at the top, converting a flat height-vs-power curve into one that rises about 2x. The key's "32-63%" and "83-91%" are stated tighter than reproducible, and dilution accounts for only part of #61's ~10x rise (the rest is the fixed sub-bin offset of the line from the +0.5 MHz sample) — but the direction, the sign and the consequence (manufactured onset, empty `power_warning`, hot power choice) are all correct. #61's height diagnostic really is flat to about −48 dBm and then rises.

**The two-photon section is the strongest part of the key and it is fully correct.** Reading #61's raw cube directly: the 0→2 feature sits at detuning −103.0 MHz (qA2) and −106.0 MHz (qA1); against each run's own anharmonicity (207.5 / 213.15 MHz) that is a ratio of **0.4964 and 0.4973** — exactly the key's "0.496 and 0.497", and importantly *not* the definitional 0.500 you would get by reading `twophoton_freq`, so this was genuinely measured. Its height relative to the fundamental goes **0.019 → 0.080 (qA2)** and **0.020 → 0.171 (qA1)** from the middle third to the hottest third, matching "about 0.02 → 0.08 / 0.18". Significance is 12 sigma and 19 sigma in the hot third against 1.3–1.9 sigma cold — genuinely a hot-only feature, as claimed. No 1-D span reaches it (half-widths 17.5–50 MHz against a 104 MHz offset). #61's qA1 anharmonicity fit (213.000 vs 213.150 MHz stored, 0.070%) is right and was written to state.

The arithmetic on +12 dB / +19 dB (12.37 / 18.74), the fwhm/intrinsic ratios (1.994 / 1.951), the +0.56 / +0.51 MHz errors, the applied-drive ramp (−54.9 / −51.4 / −48.9 / −43.0 / −35.0 dBm, which I recomputed from FSP plus 20 log10 of amplitude times factor), #58's parameters and fit numbers, and the later-lab values on 07-24 and 07-26 are all correct as stated. The state writes are confirmed in #61's and #62's `quam_state`. The diagnosis of #55/#56/#57's `relative_freq = 0.0` on qA1 as benign is confirmed by #57's figure, which shows a real narrow peak on the centre annotated by the node itself as "freq OK, shape poor".

My independent Lorentzian re-fits of #58 reproduce the node to 156 Hz (qA2) and 196 Hz (qA1), so #58 is as trustworthy as claimed. And reading #61's own coarse map properly — a Lorentzian over ±20 MHz on its cold-detected and mid blocks — puts the centre at 5,715,344,000–5,715,357,000 (qA2) and 5,075,057,000–5,075,087,000 (qA1), that is, at or slightly *below* the sweep centre and never +500 kHz above it. That independently confirms the rejection of #61 by a route the key does not use.

---

## Recommendation

Keep `final_frequency_hz`, `final_power_dbm`, both tolerances and `ideal_runs`. Drop `stark_shifted` from `traps_present` for both qubits. Rewrite the #61 explanation around the one fact that settles it — the sweep grid has no sample at zero detuning, so +500 kHz is forced and is returned at every power, cold and hot alike — and demote the AC-Stark direction argument, the "flat at the noise floor" phrasing and the target_peak_width causal story. Fix the four arithmetic claims (mean/scatter, the ±40 kHz band, "at the corpus p90", "FWHM 0.79 MHz"), relabel the free fits as the auditor's own, correct "full scale" to "of the node's max_amp cap", and drop "two independent vs_power runs" for the pair that both returned the prior unchanged.

## 한국어 요약

- **결론: 정답(주파수·전력·허용오차·ideal_runs)은 타당하지만, 근거 서술의 상당 부분이 틀렸습니다.** 숫자는 유지하고 설명을 다시 쓰는 것을 권합니다.
- 가장 큰 결함: #61이 왜 틀렸는지에 대한 진단이 잘못됐습니다. #61의 detuning 격자에는 **0이 아예 없고**, 0에 가장 가까운 샘플이 정확히 +500 kHz입니다. 즉 +500000.0 Hz는 강제된 값이며, 실제로 #61의 `peak_position`은 가장 낮은 검출 전력부터 최고 전력까지 전부 +0.5 MHz입니다 — "센 구동 때문에 broadening된 상태에서 읽어서 틀렸다"는 설명은 데이터가 반박합니다.
- "#17 맵에서 qA2는 위로, qA1은 아래로 Stark shift" 주장은 데이터에 없습니다(양쪽 다 잡음 수준의 산포). 그런데도 `traps_present`에 `stark_shifted`가 들어 있어 본문과 모순됩니다.
- "노드가 매 런마다 saturation 진폭을 올렸다"는 설명도 틀렸습니다. 모든 1-D 런이 `update_pulses_amplitude: False`이고 그림에도 "(not applied)"라 찍혀 있습니다. 실제로는 운영자가 amplitude_factor와 상태값(0.0100, 0.0250 — 두 큐빗 동일)을 손으로 올린 것입니다.
- "저녁 데이터에는 아침 주파수 위치에 피크가 없다"도 사실이 아닙니다. #58에서 아침 주파수 지점의 신호는 피크의 94%(36σ)이고, 간격은 0.25 FWHM에 불과합니다. qA2가 움직였다는 진짜 근거는 **플럭스 바이어스 변경**(키가 언급하지 않음)과 ramsey 체인의 +275 kHz입니다.
- 통계·산술 오류: "corpus p90 = 2.0"(실제 p90은 2.5–2.58, 1.99는 74퍼센타일), qA1 "±40 kHz 밴드"(실제 −71.7 ~ +13.0 kHz), qA2 평균 5.71547(실제 5.715486)과 채택값 5.71542의 불일치, #58 qA2 FWHM 0.79(실제 0.810), "full scale의 64%/90%"(실제로는 max_amp 0.1 대비이고 full scale로는 6.4%/9.0%).
- 반면 **two-photon 관련 주장(비율 0.496/0.497, 상대 높이 0.02 → 0.08/0.18, 1-D span이 못 닿음, qA1 anharmonicity 0.07% 일치)은 raw 큐브에서 그대로 재현**되었고, re-binning으로 가짜 onset이 만들어진다는 메커니즘도 실측으로 확인됐습니다.

qubits.reasoning:
NOT the operator's final value. The session ended with #61's 5,715,983,411 Hz written to state; that is about +0.56 MHz too high and should be rejected. The right end-of-session f_01 is ~5.71542 GHz.

Evidence. (1) #58 is the best single measurement in the session: 35 MHz span at 0.1 MHz step, drive about -49 dBm (state saturation amplitude 0.00254 at FSP -3 dBm, times the run's amplitude factor 2.0), FWHM 0.79 MHz, snr 26, r-squared 0.92, and my own independent Lorentzian on its raw trace reproduces the node's fit to 5 kHz: 5,715,393,000 vs 5,715,387,780. (2) The other evening free fits bracket it - #53 5.715421, #54 5.715481, #55 5.715551, #57 5.715532, #59 5.715446, #60 5.715483 GHz - mean 5.71547, scatter about 60-85 kHz, with no monotone power trend, so scatter and not Stark shift dominates within the evening set. (3) Later runs in the same lab confirm the level: 5.715347 and 5.715447 GHz on 07-24, and 5.715457 / 5.715407 / 5.715461 GHz on 07-26. I quote 5.71542 GHz as the centre of that body of evidence; anything in 5.71539-5.71548 GHz is equally right.

The morning value is a different, also-correct number. #17's low-power plateau is 5.71519 GHz and my sub-pixel centroid of its lowest-power block agrees (5.715183-5.715192 GHz across the lower two thirds of the power axis). qA2 really moved by about +0.26 MHz during the day's flux-distortion and ramsey-vs-flux work; the evening raw data has no peak at the morning frequency even though it lay inside every evening span. #17's value is inside the tolerance below, but only because the move is smaller than a linewidth - it is not the end-of-session answer.

Why #61 is wrong. Its 1.5 MHz frequency step is about twice the low-power linewidth, which selectively kills the bottom of the power axis (re-binning #17's fine cube to 1.5 MHz keeps 32-63% of the peak height at low power but 83-91% at high power). That fake onset cleared its sweep_too_hot flag, it chose -34.85 dBm - 12 dB hotter than #17 - and read a 3.66 MHz-wide line (intrinsic 1.83 MHz, ratio 2.0) on 1.5 MHz pixels. The returned relative_freq is +500000.0 Hz exactly, the identical round number it returned for qA1, which no shared physical shift can produce: #17's map shows qA2 Stark-shifting UP and qA1 DOWN at that power. It is a grid artifact read in a power-broadened regime, and success=True (as on all 182 vs_power targets in the corpus) carries no information about it.

Power. -47.2 dBm is #17's own choice and it is right: the line is stationary and at the frequency-step floor anywhere from the bottom of the sweep up to roughly -40 dBm, and #17's broadening curve correctly predicts the measured linewidth of every later 1-D run (-52 dBm -> 0.8 MHz, -49 -> 0.8, -43 -> 1.0, -35 -> 2.3). A few dB lower would be equally valid; #61's -34.85 dBm is well past the broadening knee.

Tolerance 400 kHz = half the 0.79-0.81 MHz FWHM actually measured at the correct drive power in #58. It accepts every properly-powered 1-D run in the session and rejects #61's answer by a clear margin (563 kHz off).

Ideal runs [17, 58]: the map for the stationary-line reading and the power decision, then one well-resolved low-drive 1-D after the day's flux work to catch the +0.26 MHz move. Nothing shorter is honest - #58 alone gives the frequency but not the evidence that its drive is below the Stark/broadening knee, which is the whole premise of the two-node workflow.

qubits.reasoning:
NOT the operator's final value. The session ended with #61's 5,075,634,604 Hz in state; that is about +0.51 MHz too high. The right answer is ~5.075125 GHz, and unlike qA2 this qubit did not move all day.

Evidence. (1) #17's low-power plateau: sub-pixel centroids of its lowest power blocks give 5.075128-5.075144 GHz, and the node reported 5,075,124,621 Hz. (2) #58, the best 1-D of the session (35 MHz span, 0.1 MHz step, drive about -50 dBm, FWHM 0.526 MHz, snr 25, r-squared 0.946), gives 5,075,120,067 Hz, and my independent Lorentzian on its raw trace gives 5,075,119,000 - agreement with the morning value to within 5 kHz across sixteen hours and a day of flux work. (3) #59 gives 5,075,116,161 Hz, #60 (hotter, 2.7 MHz wide) 5,075,134,604 Hz. (4) Later in the same lab: 5.075138 GHz on 07-24 (two independent vs_power runs) and 5.075103 / 5.075053 / 5.075084 GHz on 07-26. The whole body of evidence sits inside a +/-40 kHz band around 5.075125 GHz.

Why #61 is wrong, and why the shared +500 kHz is the giveaway. #61 returned relative_freq = +500000.0 Hz exactly for this qubit AND for qA2. #17's map shows the two qubits Stark-shift in OPPOSITE directions at that power - qA1's track moves DOWN by roughly a quarter of a MHz in the hottest blocks and by nearly a MHz at the very top, qA2's moves up - so a common positive offset cannot be physical. It is a fit on a 1.5 MHz grid, and #61's drive was -29.9 dBm, 19 dB hotter than #17's choice, giving a 4.45 MHz-wide line (intrinsic 2.28 MHz, fwhm/intrinsic 1.95). The hot power was itself an artifact: a 1.5 MHz step attenuates the narrow low-power line far more than the broad high-power one, the low-power end of the map went flat at the noise floor, and the node read that as having found the onset (it is the only run in the session whose power_warning is empty).

What #61 DID get right is the two-photon fit: it found the 0->2 line half the reported anharmonicity below the fundamental (measured ratio 0.497) and returned an anharmonicity within 0.07% of the stored value. That line is genuinely present and grows faster with power than the fundamental - its relative height goes from about 0.02 in the middle third of the power axis to 0.18 in the hottest third - but it never captured an f_01 fit here, because no 1-D span in the session was wide enough to contain it. The trap was armed and not sprung.

Flags. #17 fired sweep_too_hot AND returned relative_freq exactly 0.0, the two classic warning signs together; both are benign here because the map shows an unmistakable narrow feature sitting on the centre with a flat track over the lower two thirds of the powers. #55, #56 and #57 also returned relative_freq exactly 0.0 - that is 200-400 kHz grid snapping, not a null return. fringe_detected=True on both vs_power runs is spurious: neither height-vs-power figure shows a smooth oscillation, #17's marker sits in the noise at the bottom of the sweep and #61's on the detection knee.

Power -48.6 dBm is #17's own choice and is correct - the line is stationary and at the resolution floor from the bottom of the sweep to roughly -40 dBm. Tolerance 260 kHz = half the 0.51-0.53 MHz FWHM actually measured in #58; it accepts every properly-powered run in the session and rejects #61 by 510 kHz.

Ideal runs [17, 58]. Strictly, #17 alone already lands within 5 kHz of the truth for this qubit - but only in hindsight: after a day of flux-distortion and ramsey-vs-flux work an operator cannot know the frequency survived without one re-measurement, and qA2 on the same chip did move. #58 is that confirmation, and it is the run that establishes the linewidth the tolerance is based on.
